"COMPLETE GAME DESCRIPTION AND DEVELOPMENT SPECIFICATION

1. THE GAME'S CORE CONCEPT

The game is an interactive, AI-powered first-date simulator that takes place inside a restaurant. The player goes on a first date with an AI-controlled character who has their own personality, emotions, thoughts, opinions, memories, preferences, and conversational behavior. The experience should feel like going on an actual first date with another person, not communicating with a chatbot.

The entire game revolves around natural conversation, social interaction, character animation, relationship development, unexpected situations, and player decisions. The player should be able to type absolutely anything they want instead of being restricted to preset dialogue choices. The AI character must understand what the player means, recognize context, respond appropriately, and develop a natural conversational relationship throughout the date.

Every visible character in the game is a doppelganger. The game has an animated visual style, and characters should be represented through expressive, fluid animations rather than static profile pictures.

2. THE FIVE HIDDEN STAGES OF THE DATE

The date must have five distinct progression stages. These stages control the character's behavior, conversation, emotional development, and the overall atmosphere of the experience.

IMPORTANT: The player must NEVER be told which stage they are currently experiencing. There must be no visible stage counter, stage title, progression label, or announcement saying that the date has entered another stage. The player should naturally recognize the progression through the character's behavior.

STAGE 1: FIRST IMPRESSIONS
The date begins with the characters meeting and getting introduced. The atmosphere should contain some natural first-date awkwardness, curiosity, nervousness, excitement, and uncertainty. The character should introduce herself naturally, make observations, ask questions, and occasionally initiate conversation. She shouldn't immediately behave as if she knows the player extremely well. Her behavior should reflect meeting somebody for the first time.

STAGE 2: GETTING COMFORTABLE
As the conversation continues, the character gradually becomes more comfortable. She might joke more frequently, become less nervous, tease the player, share small personal details, and develop a more relaxed conversational rhythm. Her body language and facial expressions should gradually reflect her increasing comfort. She should begin showing more of her actual personality.

STAGE 3: PERSONAL AND DEEPER CONVERSATIONS
The conversation can naturally become more meaningful. The character might discuss personal experiences, relationships, memories, interests, fears, ambitions, or other subjects. She should also become interested in learning more about the player. She must remember previous answers and use them naturally. Not every conversation needs to become serious. Humor and casual discussion should remain possible.

STAGE 4: SOMETHING UNUSUAL HAPPENS
An unexpected event should interrupt or change the normal flow of the date. This could involve the waiter, something happening in the restaurant, an awkward situation, an unexpected interaction, or something related to the character. These events should make the date feel alive and unpredictable. The character must react according to her personality and current emotional state. The event should not feel like an unrelated scripted interruption.

STAGE 5: FINAL MOMENTS
The date gradually approaches its conclusion. The character's behavior should reflect everything that happened throughout the experience. She might discuss whether she enjoyed the date, bring up memorable moments, express uncertainty, show affection, or indicate that she would like to meet again. Her reaction must depend on the actual conversation and interactions, not simply the number of messages exchanged.

The five stages must be controlled by an actual progression syste

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.

const freshState=()=>({started:false,ended:false,turns:0,stage:1,comfort:0,openness:0,curiosity:0,respect:0,joy:0,depth:0,topicSet:new Set(),facts:[],moments:[],lastTopics:[],lastQuestion:'',lastReply:'',event:false,eventTurns:0,finalAsked:false,firstName:'',history:[],runStarted:0});
let game=freshState(), toastTimer, audioCtx, ambience=null;
const topics={food:/\b(food|eat|dish|menu|drink|wine|coffee|cook|restaurant|order|dessert|hungry|taste|favorite meal)\b/i,work:/\b(work|job|career|office|colleague|boss|study|school|class|university|profess|design|write|engineer|nurse|teach)\b/i,travel:/\b(travel|trip|visit|country|city|vacation|holiday|abroad|flight|beach|mountain|road trip)\b/i,hobby:/\b(hobby|music|book|read|film|movie|art|paint|dance|run|hike|game|guitar|concert|weekend|free time)\b/i,family:/\b(family|parent|mother|mom|father|dad|sister|brother|childhood|grew up|home town|grandma|grandmother)\b/i,relationship:/\b(relationship|love|dating|date|ex\b|partner|marriage|commitment|romantic|breakup|heartbreak)\b/i,values:/\b(dream|afraid|fear|hope|future|ambition|meaning|proud|regret|believe|important to me|wish|change)\b/i,feelings:/\b(feel|nervous|anxious|happy|sad|lonely|excited|stress|hard|difficult|tough|worried|grateful)\b/i,flirt:/\b(cute|beautiful|pretty|handsome|attractive|chemistry|kiss|flirt|charming|gorgeous)\b/i};
const replies={
food:['I almost ordered the mushroom pasta, but then I saw the roasted pear salad and lost my nerve. Are you a safe-order person or a try-something-weird person?','The kitchen sent out this little olive thing while I was waiting. I have decided it counts as dinner. work:['I do editorial illustration—mostly books and the occasional very serious magazine article. It’s lovely until a deadline starts making eye contact. travel:['I took a train up the coast last spring and got off at the wrong stop. It turned out to be the nicest afternoon of the trip. Do you like having a plan when you travel?','I keep saying I’ll go to Lisbon, then I spend my vacation somewhere I can reach on one tank of gas. What place has stayed with you?','I’m happiest somewhere walkable, with a bookshop and no itinerary. Is there a place you’d go back to in a heartbeat?'],
hobby:['Lately I’ve been trying to keep a tiny balcony garden alive. The basil and I are not on speaking terms. What do you do when nobody needs anything from you?','I’ve been listening to the same album on repeat while I draw. It’s either comforting or a cry for help. What have you been into lately?','I go to a little cinema that still has an intermission. I love having time to argue with myself about the ending. What kind of stories do you get pulled into?'],
family:['My family is the kind that sends a photo of a very ordinary sandwich and expects a review. I miss them more than I admit. What was home like for you?','My sister still calls me when she can’t decide what to wear, as if I have ever made a good decision. Are you close with your family?'],
relationship:['I think I’ve learned that being able to laugh together matters more than having the same favorite everything. And that you can tell a lot by how someone treats a waiter. What feels important to you?','I used to think the right person would make everything feel effortless. Now I think it’s more about being able to be honest when it isn’t. Is that too earnest for dinner?','I’m a little out of practice at first dates, if I’m honest. But I like the possibility of meeting somebody who makes the ordinary bits fun. What do you think makes a connection work?'],
values:['I’d like to make things that make somebody feel a little less alone. That sounds grand; most days it means finishing one drawing. What do you hope there’s more of in your life?','I’m still figuring that out. I used to think there was supposed to be one big answer, but lately the smaller things feel truer. What’s something you want to make room for?','That’s a real question. I think I’m afraid of waking up one day and realizing I’ve been too careful. What’s a risk you’re glad you took?'],
feelings:['Thanks for telling me. I know it can feel strange saying something real to someone you just met. What’s been helping you through it?','I get that. I don’t want to rush past it—what part has been on your mind most?'],
flirt:['You say that like you’re trying to make me blush. It’s working a little. function topicOf(text){for(const [k,re] of Object.entries(topics))if(re.test(text))return k;return 'general'}
function extractFact(text){const clean=text.trim().replace(/[.!?].*$/,'').slice(0,86);const m=clean.match(/\b(?:i am|i'm|i work as|i work in|i live in|i grew up in|i love|i like|i enjoy|i have|my favorite is|my family|i used to)\s+(.+)/i);if(!m)return;const fact=m[0].replace(/^i'm\b/i,'I am').trim();if(fact.length>5&&!game.facts.some(x=>x.toLowerCase()===fact.toLowerCase())){game.facts.push(fact);if(game.facts.length>6)game.facts.shift()}}
function sentiment(text){const pos=/\b(love|like|great|good|fun|enjoy|happy|excited|nice|beautiful|amazing|wonderful|yes|glad|sweet|laugh|agree|interesting|thank|kind|cute)\b/i.test(text);const neg=/\b(hate|awful|boring|stupid|shut up|idiot|ugly|annoying|whatever|don't care|gross|dumb|leave me|worthless)\b/i.test(text);return pos&&!neg?1:neg?-2:0}
function detectName(text){const m=text.match(/(?:i am|i'm|call me)\s+([A-Z][a-z]{1,14})\b/);if(m)game.firstName=m[1]}
function responseFor(text,topic){const lower=text.toLowerCase();const flirt=topic==='flirt';const q=topic==='relationship'&&/\b(you|your)\b/.test(lower);let line='';if(/\b(what|how|where|why|when|who) (do|did|are|is|was|were|have|has|would|could|can|will) you\b/.test(lower)||/\btell me about yourself\b/.test(lower)){if(/favorite|favourite/.test(lower))line='I have a very serious weakness for late-night pancakes, which feels like an embarrassing answer in a restaurant this nice. What about you?';else if(/dream|hope|want|future|afraid/.test(lower))line='I want to make work I’m proud of and still have a life that isn’t just work. I’m trying to get better at leaving room for the unplanned bits. What about you?';else if(/first date|dating|relationship/.test(lower))line='I’m hoping for curious and kind. A little awkward is fine—I think that’s how you know it’s a real person across from you. What about you?';else line='I’m an illustrator, I get too attached to houseplants, and I think the best conversations happen when nobody is checking the time. I’m still figuring out the rest. What would you like to know?'}
if(!line){if(topic!=='general'){const arr=replies[topic]||generic;line=arr[(game.turns*3+game.topicSet.size)%arr.length]}else if(/\b(hello|hi|hey|nice to meet|how are you)\b/.test(lower))line='I’m good—nervous enough that I may have read the menu upside down, but in a good way. How was getting here?';else if(/\b(thank you|thanks)\b/.test(lower))line='You’re welcome. I like that you noticed. So—tell me something I wouldn’t guess just by looking at you.';else if(/\b(sorry|apologize|my bad)\b/.test(lower))line='Hey, it’s okay. First dates are strange little performances until they aren’t. We can just talk.';else if(/\b(joke|funny|laugh)\b/.test(lower))line='Okay, that got me. I was trying to play it cool and now I’m smiling at my water glass. Your turn—do you have a go-to terrible joke?';else line=generic[(game.turns*7+text.length)%generic.length]}
if(q&&game.openness>2)line+=' I don’t always tell people that this early, but you make it feel easy.';
if(game.facts.length&&game.turns%3===0){const f=game.facts[(game.turns/3|0)%game.facts.length];line=`I keep thinking about what you said—that ${f.replace(/^I am /i,'you are ').replace(/^I /i,'you ')}. ${line}`}
if(game.stage>=2&&game.comfort>4&&game.turns%3===1)line=line.replace(/What about you\?/,'And I’m curious what you think.').replace(/What do you think\?/,'I have a feeling you have a good answer.');
if(game.stage>=3&&game.depth>1&&game.turns%2===0&&topic!=='feelings'&&topic!=='values')line+=' I like that we can wander a bit with this.';
if(game.event&&game.eventTurns<3&&game.turns%2===0)line+=' I keep smiling about the whole room going dark. A strange little thing to share with someone you just met.';
return line}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable first-date simulator set in a restaurant, with freeform conversation, expressive animated characters, relationship development, an unexpected event, and a nuanced ending.

## Requirements
- The player must be able to type anything; the date should respond contextually and remember details.
- Use five hidden progression stages; never show stage labels, counters, or announcements.
- Character behavior, emotions, animation, and ending should reflect conversation and player decisions.
- All visible characters are doppelgangers; animated visuals rather than static profile pictures.
- Build now without clarification. Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Implemented a self-contained browser game in one HTML file, with local heuristic conversation instead of an external AI service.
- Progression uses rapport, conversation topics, and disclosure rather than message count alone; stage indicators remain hidden.
- Character visuals are original inline SVG with CSS animation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the playable game in `index.html`: restaurant scene, animated character, unrestricted text input, contextual replies, remembered details, hidden progression, unexpected power outage, sound toggle, and relationship-aware ending.
- Ran `node --check` on the extracted script successfully.
- Started a local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Opened the app in Playwright and saved/read a screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/after-hours.jpg`.

### Active
- None.

### Blocked
- Browser check reported one console error; its cause has not been inspected yet.
- No further gameplay interaction or responsive/mobile checks have been completed.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the browser console error and fix it if it is caused by the game.
2. Exercise conversation, hidden progression/event, and ending in the browser; check a mobile viewport.
3. Report the local heuristic conversation limitation and other reasonable assumptions briefly when finishing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `index.html` is newly created.
- Browser opened at `http://localhost:3002`; Playwright Chromium was installed after the initial launch failed with `Browser "chromium" is not installed`.
